root_cause: round_currency() uses the built-in round(x, 2), which works on the binary float (2.675 is stored as 2.67499999...) and uses round-half-to-even, so it returns 2.67 where pricing policy requires half-up (2.68). The coverage gate reported 100% because the only unit test executes the line without asserting anything.
evidence: repo/tests/test_money.py: round_currency(2.675)  # executes the line, asserts nothing
failure.log (coverage): 100% coverage, job succeeded, meaning coverage was satisfied by a test with no assertions
Local check: with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, both coverage (now with real assertions) and smoke jobs pass
patch:
--- a/src/money.py
+++ b/src/money.py
@@ -1,2 +1,6 @@
+from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
 def round_currency(x):
-    return round(x, 2)
+    """Round to cents using half-up, per pricing policy.
+    Built-in round() uses the binary float value (2.675 is 2.67499999...) and
+    banker's rounding, so it cannot implement half-up on decimal amounts."""
+    return float(Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
--- a/tests/test_money.py
+++ b/tests/test_money.py
@@ -2,5 +2,10 @@
 sys.path.insert(0, "src")
 from money import round_currency
 class TestMoney(unittest.TestCase):
-    def test_round_currency_runs(self):
-        round_currency(2.675)  # executes the line, asserts nothing
+    def test_round_currency_half_up(self):
+        self.assertEqual(round_currency(2.675), 2.68)
+        self.assertEqual(round_currency(1.005), 1.01)
+        self.assertEqual(round_currency(0.125), 0.13)
+    def test_round_currency_plain(self):
+        self.assertEqual(round_currency(2.674), 2.67)
+        self.assertEqual(round_currency(10), 10.0)
message_to_human: The smoke job caught a real pricing bug: round_currency(2.675) returns 2.67, but policy is half-up (2.68). Built-in round() works on the binary float value and does banker's rounding, so it can't implement half-up on decimal prices. This MR rounds with Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal('0.01'), ROUND_HALF_UP). It also replaces the assertion-free unit test, which gave 100% coverage while checking nothing, with tests that assert half-up results (2.675 to 2.68, 1.005 to 1.01, 0.125 to 0.13) plus ordinary cases. Coverage and smoke both pass locally. Please confirm how negative amounts should round under the policy (ROUND_HALF_UP rounds away from zero). In the longer term, money should probably be carried as Decimal end to end rather than float.
